sources.title: Mobile Infrastructure Project Impact and Benefits Report
facts: Published 11 October 2017 and reports outcomes, benefits and cost effectiveness.
The project delivered 2G, 3G and 4G through 75 masts to 7,199 premises previously without mobile signal.
The evaluation found delivery costs below expectations and value for money above the re-baselined business case estimate.

sources.title: Broadband Connection Voucher Scheme Impact and Benefits Study
facts: The scheme ran from March 2014 to March 2016 and subsidised upfront connection costs.
It expanded to 50 cities and surrounding areas with £40 million of challenge funding.
More than 40,000 small and medium-sized businesses received a faster connection through the scheme.

sources.title: The UK's National Broadband Scheme - an independent evaluation
facts: Published 19 May 2015 and commissioned from Oxera by BDUK.
The evaluation tests State aid compliance, effectiveness and potential competition or trade distortion.
It supports review of the scheme framework rather than current premises-level service status.

sources.title: State Aid consultation: Market Test Pilot Intervention Areas
facts: The publication concerns a State Aid consultation for superfast broadband Market Test Pilots.
It was first published in 2014 and updated in 2015.
Consultation intervention areas are historical policy inputs, not current coverage evidence.

sources.title: UK Broadband Impact Study - Baseline Report
facts: The baseline report establishes reference conditions for the UK Broadband Impact Study.
Baseline measures must be interpreted with their original period and methodology.
A baseline is not a current service or address-level availability record.

sources.title: UK Broadband Impact Study
facts: The study assesses broadband impacts using the programme's defined analytical framework.
Results are historical impact evidence and require their original geography and period.
Study estimates cannot substitute for a current provider orderability check.

sources.title: UK broadband impact study: literature review
facts: The literature review synthesises existing evidence for the UK Broadband Impact Study.
It is secondary evidence used to inform impact assumptions and methods.
Literature findings must not be represented as measured current parcel facts.

sources.title: The Benefits and Challenges of 4G Connectivity in Rural Scotland
facts: The report is a qualitative exploration of 4G connectivity in rural Scotland.
It covers benefits, disbenefits and infrastructure-related experiences.
Qualitative findings describe participant experience and are not a statistical coverage map.

sources.title: Beyond the digital divide
facts: Published 27 November 2024 and examines poor connectivity affecting rural farmers.
It proposes a digital-needs hierarchy for identifying and measuring connectivity benefits.
The research framework is not an exact UPRN or service-orderability dataset.

sources.title: Blackpool - Connectivity and Tourism. A LFFN case study
facts: BDUK researchers interviewed Blackpool Council, hotel proprietors and guests in summer 2021.
The case study links LFFN infrastructure with local economic, tourism and public-service strategies.
Case-study findings are local and qualitative rather than nationally generalisable coverage measures.

sources.title: Benefits of Rural Mobile Coverage
facts: BDUK used about 1,000 online surveys and five follow-up interviews.
The report examines daily challenges in mobile not-spots and likely benefits from improved coverage.
Expected benefits include work satisfaction, safety, economic growth and wellbeing.

sources.title: Connecting gigabit communities and rural schools: the gigabit journey
facts: The research covers rural primary schools receiving gigabit-capable Hub connections.
Methods include surveys, interviews and observations from March 2020 to January 2021.
Findings include peer support, public value, inclusion and effects of poor connectivity on staff wellbeing.

sources.title: Benefits of high speed internet: case study research
facts: The publication presents case-study research on benefits associated with high-speed internet.
Case studies provide contextual qualitative evidence rather than a complete population measure.
Any use must preserve the studied locations, participants and observation periods.

sources.title: What happens next? Mapping the route from digital infrastructure to digital inclusion
facts: The report maps pathways from digital infrastructure to digital inclusion.
It examines public-sector buildings and uses social-media material to identify actors supporting devices and skills.
The research concerns inclusion pathways, not current broadband service availability.
